generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia, Fagaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves often lobed. Wikipedia, Oak: many lobed, others merely toothed or smooth. DELTA, Fagaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade undivided or cut (pinnatifid). Weighted by genus size: Lithocarpus, Castanopsis, Fagus, Castanea and many evergreen oaks are unlobed; lobing mostly in deciduous Quercus. The library leans to Quercus, where lobed is commoner.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 282, 284: perianth 5- to 6-merous in two whorls, e.g. Castanea K3+3 (3 per whorl); Quercus 4- to 5-merous. Simpson p. 337: 6, rarely 4 to 9, tepals.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337: stamens 6 to 12, rarely 4 to 90.

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337: female flowers epigynous with an inferior ovary (Floral Diagrams p. 282 also inferior).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337, 505: Simpson calls the female flowers epigynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 62 Fagaceae: trees; leaves alternate, simple, pinnately veined; stipules present, often soon falling; flowers unisexual on the same tree, the male in erect or catkin-like spikes; calyx 4- to 6-lobed, no petals; ovary inferior, 3- to 6-celled; fruit a nut in a cup or husk (involucre). Hutchinson's Fagaceae held Nothofagus, now its own family.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia Fagaceae (read 2026-10-17): temperate members mostly deciduous, many tropical ones evergreen and dominant in East Asian subtropical forest. Genus sizes from the same page: Lithocarpus c. 330-340 and Castanopsis c. 125-130 (evergreen) plus the evergreen share of Quercus (c. 600; live oaks, ring-cup oaks) outweigh deciduous Quercus with Fagus (10-13) and Castanea (8). Re-ranks the earlier value, from watson-dallwitz-1992, whose top states were tied.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337, 339, family Fagaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337, 339, family Fagaceae: leaf arrangement alternate (spiral; rarely opposite or whorled), usually; read as {"alternate": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Fagaceae (read 2026-10-17): unisexual flowers borne in catkins. Quercus (c. 600) has hanging catkins; the erect spikes of Lithocarpus and Castanopsis (c. 460) kept at often; heads only in Fagus (10-13 spp.), so sometimes. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337, 339, family Fagaceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic; read as "actinomorphic".
